quizName: DMV Practice Test #10 25 Questions • Passing Score 21

questions.question: Is it legal to ride between two vehicles moving in the same direction?

options.text: Yes, during the day to help traffic flow.
Yes, if the rider is comfortable doing it.

questions.explanation: In Oregon, motorcycles and mopeds cannot ride between two moving vehicles on a multilane highway or one-way street.

questions.question: What should you tell a passenger before riding?

options.text: Sit as far back as possible.
Put their feet on the muffler.
Get on the motorcycle after you start the engine.

questions.correctAnswerText: Get on the motorcycle after you start the engine.
questions.explanation: Always give your passenger complete safety instructions before riding. Tell them to get on only after you start the engine. They should sit as far forward as possible without crowding you and hold onto your waist, hips, or belt. They must keep both feet on the footrests at all times, even when stopped.

questions.question: Where is the clutch lever on a motorcycle?
questions.explanation: The clutch lever is located on the left handgrip of a motorcycle.

questions.question: What lane position should riders use?

options.text: Pick one lane position and always use it.
Change lane positions often to stay alert.
Choose the position that gives you the most space around you.
Never use the center lane position.

questions.correctAnswerText: Choose the position that gives you the most space around you.
questions.explanation: Road and traffic conditions change constantly. Choose the lane position that gives you the most space around you and makes it easiest for other drivers to see you.

questions.question: Most motorcycle crashes happen during the day. What should you do?

options.text: Do not ride during the day.
Ride on the shoulder away from traffic.

questions.explanation: Most motorcycle crashes happen in daylight. Wear bright clothing whenever you ride so other drivers can see you, even during the day.

questions.question: How do headache, cold, and hay fever medications affect your body?

options.text: They make it hard to focus.

questions.explanation: Most medications for headaches, colds, hay fever, allergies, or stress can make you drowsy and hurt your ability to ride safely. Always know how a medication affects you before riding.

questions.question: When turning on a motorcycle, what should you do?

options.text: Turn your head and shoulders to look through the turn.
Keep your knees away from the gas tank.
Turn only your head to look through the turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn only your head to look through the turn.
questions.explanation: When turning, look through the turn by turning only your head. Keep your knees against the gas tank for balance. Your arms should be slightly bent when holding the handlebars.

questions.question: How should you stop quickly on wet pavement?
questions.explanation: Use both brakes when you need to stop quickly on a wet surface. You can safely use the front brake on wet pavement if you apply it gradually to avoid locking the wheel.

questions.question: How much of a motorcycle's stopping power comes from the front brake?
questions.explanation: The front brake is more powerful than the rear brake. It provides at least 70 percent of a motorcycle's total stopping power.

questions.question: What should you do before changing lanes?

options.text: Turn your head to check for vehicles in your blind spot.
Use only your mirrors to see all around you.
Point in the direction you are changing lanes.
Speed up to get ahead of other vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your head to check for vehicles in your blind spot.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles have blind spots just like other vehicles. Always turn your head to check your blind spot before changing lanes. Do not rely on mirrors alone.

questions.question: If your friend has been drinking alcohol, which of the following should you NOT do?

options.text: Arrange a safe ride home for your friend.
Keep your friend busy with activities to slow their drinking.
Keep your friend from leaving until they are sober.
Allow your friend to ride their motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Allow your friend to ride their motorcycle.
questions.explanation: You can prevent an impaired friend from riding by arranging safe transportation, keeping them occupied with other activities, and not letting them leave until they are sober. You can also ask other friends to help stop them.

questions.question: Making eye contact with another driver:

options.text: Guarantees that the other driver will yield to you.
Does not guarantee that the other driver will yield to you.
Means the other driver sees you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Does not guarantee that the other driver will yield to you.
questions.explanation: Never assume that eye contact with another driver means they will give you the right-of-way. You cannot depend on it.

questions.question: To increase your chances of being seen at an intersection, you should:

options.text: Try to make eye contact with other drivers.
Ride as close as possible to the vehicle ahead.

questions.explanation: The best way to be seen at an intersection is to ride with your headlight on. Keep your headlight on whenever your motorcycle is running.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a safe way to prevent fatigue while riding?

options.text: Protect yourself from wind, cold, and rain.
Limit how far you ride in one day.

questions.explanation: On long trips, take frequent breaks and do not ride more than six hours in one day. Wear clothing to protect yourself from the elements. Do not use artificial stimulants because they can be dangerous when they wear off.

questions.question: To control your motorcycle well, you should:

options.text: Use your arms to prop yourself up, not to steer.
Keep your knees against the gas tank for balance.
Let your feet hang off the footrests.
Sit far back so you must stretch to reach the handgrips.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your knees against the gas tank for balance.
questions.explanation: Keep your knees against the gas tank to help balance during turns. Sit forward enough that your arms are slightly bent when you hold the handgrips. Use your arms to steer, not to support yourself. Keep your feet firmly on the footrests.

questions.question: Riding in cold weather for long periods could cause all of the following, except:
questions.explanation: Riding in cold weather for long periods can cause fatigue, severe chills, and hypothermia. Wear proper clothing to protect yourself from the cold.

questions.question: On average, the body eliminates how many alcoholic drinks per hour?
questions.explanation: On average, the body eliminates about one drink per hour. The time it takes to lower blood alcohol content varies. It is safest not to ride after drinking any amount of alcohol.

questions.question: A rectangular sign may be a:
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs like speed limit signs are rectangular with white backgrounds and black lettering or symbols. You must follow the rules shown on these signs.

questions.question: Which type of sign is yellow with black lettering or symbols?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They alert you to upcoming road conditions.

questions.question: A skidding rear tire:

options.text: Eliminates your ability to change direction.
Is only a concern if the front tire is also skidding.

questions.correctAnswerText: Eliminates your ability to change direction.
questions.explanation: A skidding rear tire is dangerous and can cause a serious crash. Too much rear brake pressure locks the rear wheel and removes your ability to steer. Release the brake to regain control.

questions.question: What protects your eyes from the wind?
questions.explanation: Goggles protect your eyes from wind. Windshields, eyeglasses, and sunglasses do not provide enough protection for riders.

questions.question: What happens to a sidecar when a motorcycle accelerates?

options.text: It feels like it is lagging behind.
It feels like it is accelerating faster than the motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: It feels like it is lagging behind.
questions.explanation: A sidecar is an unpowered weight attached to your motorcycle. When you accelerate, it lags behind because of its weight and inertia.

questions.question: What should a motorcyclist do when riding near stopped or slow-moving cars?

options.text: Pull over and wait until traffic begins to move.
Ride on the shoulder to pass quickly.
Weave between cars to pass quickly.

questions.explanation: Weaving between parked or slow cars is dangerous. Car doors may open, or cars may suddenly move into traffic. You will not have space to escape. Never ride on the shoulder—other drivers will not expect you there.

questions.question: Which is not protective riding gear?

options.text: Boots that go above the ankle

questions.explanation: Good protective gear includes a jacket and pants made of leather or another tough material, boots that cover and support your ankles, and hearing protection.

questions.question: How many brakes do most motorcycles have?

options.text: Brakes in both the front and rear
Three brakes: front, rear, and emergency

questions.correctAnswerText: Brakes in both the front and rear
questions.explanation: Most motorcycles have two brakes—one for the front wheel and one for the rear wheel.
